spec: npx bootstrapper main-module guard realpaths both sides; runs main() under a .bin symlink

behaviors.behavior: isMainModule() returns true when argv[1] is a SYMLINK to the module (the npx .bin case the old guard missed)
behaviors.evidence: bootstrapper/test/bin-main-guard.test.mjs 'true when argv[1] is a SYMLINK to the module' (CI-Linux; skipped on Windows without symlink privilege)

behaviors.behavior: isMainModule() true for the real module path; false for undefined/empty and unrelated paths (import stays side-effect-free)
behaviors.evidence: bin-main-guard.test.mjs unit cases: real-path true, no-argv false, unrelated-path false — PASSED

behaviors.behavior: symmetric fallback: a non-realpath-able argv[1] resolves via path.resolve on BOTH sides (no mixed realpath/resolve branch that would re-introduce the silent no-op)
behaviors.evidence: bin-main-guard.test.mjs 'false for an unrelated path' passes a does-not-exist path, exercising the catch/path.resolve branch -> false; PASSED

behaviors.behavior: the bin executed THROUGH a symlink runs main() and prints --version (the field npx invocation the old guard silently made a no-op)
the PACKED tarball (bin/ + lib/ via the files whitelist) runs main() through a node_modules/.bin symlink
behaviors.evidence: bin-main-guard.test.mjs 'npm pack -> extract -> node <.bin symlink> --version' (CI-Linux); pack/extract/run mechanics cross-checked on Windows without the symlink step
